rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so this experiment establishes a baseline for RNA-only models with PCA encoding and single-profile setting. Testing this simple configuration clarifies the baseline performance before exploring more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations. It is the best use of the first experiment to set a reference point for comparison.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with the same RNA encoder (pca_n2000) but uses avgpool aggregation, which could improve performance by leveraging multiple profiles. It clarifies whether multiprofile settings outperform singleprofile, a key design choice. This is the best next step to explore profile settings while keeping other factors constant.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile RNA-only with avgpool aggregation (config_002) achieves higher accuracy (0.59) than singleprofile (config_001). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation improves performance in the multiprofile RNA-only setting, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploitation of the promising multiprofile direction with exploration of a key design choice.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002, 0.590664 accuracy) outperforms singleprofile and other aggregation methods. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more advanced representation) in the multiprofile setup improves accuracy, isolating the effect of representation choice. This balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of a promising design change.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (config_005) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6501). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (while keeping rna_only, multiprofile, and scvi_n200) improves accuracy. It clarifies the impact of aggregation methods on performance, balancing exploitation of the current top-performing RNA encoder with exploration of alternative aggregation strategies.

Existing evidence shows scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation (config_006) achieves the highest RNA-only accuracy. This experiment tests combining this strong RNA encoder with image data using transformer aggregation and concat fusion, which could reveal if multimodal approaches improve performance. It isolates the effect of adding image modality to the best RNA-only configuration, balancing exploration of multimodal potential with exploitation of proven RNA encoder strengths.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models (e.g., config_038) outperform rna_only/image_only baselines. The top accuracy (0.7207) uses scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion. This experiment tests whether switching fusion from concat to weighted (a critical design choice) improves performance, while keeping other components consistent. It directly addresses uncertainty about fusion method effectiveness with minimal changes, leveraging strong prior evidence for scvi_n200 and transformer.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l, using transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_039), achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.724989). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt (a more advanced model) while retaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of the RNA encoder and leverages the already proven effectiveness of transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, balancing exploitation of promising components with exploration of a new encoder.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder achieve the highest accuracy (0.724989 in config_039). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder, aggregation, and fusion method (transformer and concat) to evaluate if changing the RNA encoder impacts performance. It clarifies the effect of RNA encoder choice while keeping other factors constant, which is critical for determining if scgpt could outperform scvi_n200 in this context.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.724989 in config_039). This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoder pair with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion, which could clarify whether avgpool aggregation improves upon the transformer aggregation used in config_039. This comparison isolates the effect of aggregation method, a key design choice, and provides critical evidence to confirm if the current best configuration is robust or if alternative aggregation strategies could yield higher accuracy.
